text:
ryan: paging oncall  were seeing a surge of 500s from the /v1/embeddings endpoint across eu-central-1 and ap-southeast-1 starting ~14:07 UTC. Logs show 'variant_incompatible_error: expected embed, got chat'.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: Page routed to oncall (ryan). Incident channel created. Severity P1 for customer-facing impact.

tasha: I'm seeing the same in metrics. 5xx rate jumped to 22% for embeddings. Traces show requests routed to model 'rwd-metadata-v2:chat' for the embeddings alias.

mike: Did anyone change alias mappings or the alias->model table? I pushed an alias rotation in the rollout earlier for a canary and I thought I scoped it to 'inference-canary' only.

ryan: Looking at the alias-mapping service audit: at 14:02 UTC a rollout job applied a mapping that included a blanket alias rule for 'rwd-embeddings' pointing to 'rwd-metadata-v2' but omitted the variant tag, so default fallback picked the chat variant. The job used the new automated alias-syncer.

ops-bot: New event: alias-syncer applied mapping (job id sync-9987) by CI pipeline.

tasha: Ugh. The syncer didn't set a variant and the system default is to use 'primary' which resolves to chat for rwd-metadata-v2. That caused cross-endpoint routing.

mike: Can we short-circuit at the routing tier? I propose two mitigations: 1) pin embeddings alias explicitly to embed variant 2) change fallback policy to fail-fast for this alias so we don't attempt cross-variant fallbacks or region reroutes.

ryan: Agreed. Also throttle the alias-syncer push and add a guardrail. I'll apply a quick fix.

deploy-bot: Starting quick rollback: applying alias patch by ryan.

ryan: Patch I applied:
```
PATCH /internal/alias-config HTTP/1.1
Host: config.internal
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "alias": "rwd-embeddings",
  "model": "rwd-metadata-v2",
  "variant": "embed",
  "fallback_policy": "fail_on_incompatible"
}
```

ops-bot: Config patch applied in eu-central-1 and ap-southeast-1.

tasha: eu-central stabilized within 40s. ap-southeast still showing elevated errors; looks like route cache in regional proxies had TTL 300s.

mike: Kicked the regional proxy cache invalidation and restarted the routing agent on ap-southeast-1 node pool (rolling restart). Command:
```
kubectl -n routing rollout restart daemonset/routing-agent --selector=region=ap-southeast-1
```

ops-bot: Routing agents restarted. Cache invalidation acknowledged.

ryan: Post-mitigation metrics: 5xx for embeddings back to baseline in both regions. Total customer failures estimated ~12 minutes for some enterprise tenants.

customer-ops: We have three customers (Acme Analytics, DataSpark, Kronos.ai) reporting failed embedding calls; SLA alert was triggered for Acme Analytics. Notified account teams.

mike: Root cause summary so far: alias-syncer applied a mapping without explicit variant tag -> default resolution picked chat variant. Secondary cause: permissive fallback and long regional route-cache TTL amplified blast radius.

ryan: Immediate action items:
- ryan: add a safety check to alias-syncer to refuse mappings without explicit variant when alias type is embeddings (PR rwd/alias-sync#834)
- tasha: lower route-cache TTL for alias lookups to 45s and add manual invalidation endpoint (INF-2205)
- mike: add config-level lint to CI that rejects alias patches missing variant for typed aliases (PR infra/config-lint#412)
- customer-ops: send timeline and customer impact note to affected accounts (draft ready)

mike: I opened PRs: https://git.internal/rwd/alias-sync/pull/834 and infra lint at https://git.internal/infra/config-lint/pull/412. Tests added to cover missing-variant case.

ops-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated.

ryan: Post-incident notes: total customer-facing outage window ~12-14 minutes for embeddings in two regions, no data exfiltration, no model-output integrity issues. We should consider changing default variant resolution to conservative (reject) for typed aliases.

customer-ops: Notifications sent to customers at 14:40 UTC with summary and next steps.

tasha: Follow-up tasks created: INF-2205 (cache TTL), RND-901 (change default variant resolution), SEC-2303 (audit alias-syncer permissions).

mike: We'll add an automated integration test that simulates the alias-syncer applying a mapping and validates end-to-end route resolution before commit.

ryan: Thanks team. I'll draft the incident timeline and upload trace samples to the postmortem doc. Incident closed in channel at 15:06 UTC.

infra-bot: Incident closed and linked to postmortem doc: https://postmortems.internal/incidents/1765432109

customer-ops: Final note: customers acknowledged the email, one requested a follow-up call which we scheduled for tomorrow.
